title: Transient private user-source admission implementation
purpose: Add a separate fail-closed transient admission authority for user-provided private learning sources and allow M3.3 review handoff to consume it without weakening or modifying curated benchmark SourceAdmission.
invariants: Curated benchmark SourceAdmission and benchmark_sources_v1.json remain byte-unchanged upstream authorities.
Transient admission is a separate authority and never infers permission, provenance or legal rights from upload presence, filename, URL, institution or document content.

Transient PASS requires explicit user declaration, user-provided provenance, private-personal-learning context, transient-only retention, prohibited source redistribution and legalRightsVerified=false.

Transient PASS states only that the declared private/transient processing contract is complete and exact source bytes/version are bound; it does not certify copyright, ownership, licence or legal redistribution rights.
Policy-invalid transient declarations hold before source bytes are read.
Exact source bytes and declaration are bound by deterministic SHA-256 identities and admission reproduction is host-path independent.
M3.3 prepare-review accepts either current benchmark SourceAdmission or transient user-source admission through the same --admission boundary.
Transient M3.3 handoffs contain no source-catalog.json unless at least one benchmark SourceAdmission is also present.
Reviewer independence, exact target binding, deterministic ZIP semantics and FactoryRun re-entry remain unchanged.
No persistent source catalog, source repository corpus, backend, network call, provider integration, OCR, learner-runtime change or kit-schema change is introduced.
requiredEvidence: Repository governance PASS and PR scope PASS.
Existing M3.2, M3.2.5, benchmark SourceAdmission and M3.3 regression suites remain PASS.
Explicit valid transient declaration plus exact bytes yields PASS_TRANSIENT_SOURCE_ADMISSION_V1.
Invalid declaration policy holds before bytes are read.
Same declaration and bytes at different host paths yield identical admissionId.
One-byte source drift and declaration drift fail closed.
Transient review handoff is byte-deterministic under host-path relocation.
Transient handoff omits benchmark source catalog and verifies exact admission/source binding.
Benchmark review handoff still embeds and verifies the exact benchmark catalog.
Transient review handoff consumes an independent semantic review into a self-verifying FactoryRun.
Static scan shows no network/provider/persistent source-store primitive.
Independent contradictory QA binds the exact frozen product HEAD.
adversarialTests: Valid declaration with missing source bytes.
One-byte source drift after transient admission.
Transient admission sourceId differs from handoff binding.
Transient admission attempts to masquerade as benchmark SourceAdmission.
Benchmark admission without embedded benchmark source catalog.
Source catalog embedded when no benchmark admission is present.
A transient sourceId accepted by admission must also be valid at the mandatory M3.3 SOURCE_ID=PATH boundary.
Transient sourceId length must be bounded so every admitted identity can be materialized by M3.3 without exceeding common filename-component limits.
M3.3 must resolve each source artifact by exact deterministic member path, never loose sourceId prefix matching.
Multi-source M3.3 bindings must reject sourceIds that collide under case folding before temporary materialization.
Transient admission must reject Windows reserved device stems before reading source bytes.
independentReview: A new disjoint QA package must attack the exact frozen ATLAS-WP-023 product head and may not repair product files.
QA must explicitly attack false PASS, byte/declaration drift, benchmark-regression and handoff-context confusion.
Promotion requires at least one exact transient user-source handoff path and one unchanged benchmark handoff path.

qaRound1.cause: Transient sourceId grammar accepted ':' while mandatory M3.2/M3.3 SOURCE_ID=PATH grammar rejected it.

repair.strategy: Resolve M3.3 source artifacts only by exact deterministic member names; reject case-insensitive sourceId collisions at binding parse time; reject Windows reserved transient source stems before admission; preserve bounded transient grammar and all benchmark authorities.

qaRound2.cause: Unbounded sourceId grammar permits a 300-character identifier that passes transient admission and M3.2/M3.3 parsing but fails M3.3 temporary file materialization with ENAMETOOLONG.

findings.cause: M3.3 source artifact verification used loose startswith(sourceId) lookup, so valid IDs Course and Course.pdf became ambiguous for PDF source members.
Actual Windows QA reproduced case-fold aliasing for CourseA/coursea during M3.3 temporary source materialization, causing FactoryContext rebuild mismatch.

rollback: Remove transient_source_admission.py and its tests, restore handoff.py/README/test/workflow to the promoted M3.3 behavior, and remove ATLAS-WP-023 metadata. Curated benchmark SourceAdmission, M3.2/M3.2.5, M3.4 and learner runtime remain unchanged.
